How it works

Four stages, and a hard rule underneath all of them: the reasoning model can propose anything. It can execute nothing the Authority Engine hasn't approved.

01 — Detect

RESOLVE watches the real transaction

Not a support inbox. Real carrier tracking, real merchant order status, real payment confirmations — checked continuously against what you were promised.

01

02 — Negotiate

Two bounded agents settle it directly

Your Buyer Agent and the merchant's own Merchant Agent exchange evidence and offers — each with its own hard spend ceiling — instead of a human on either end.

02

03 — Execute

The fix runs on real payment rails

A refund, a replacement, or a bounded top-up payment — executed through Razorpay, with every action checked against your authority first.

03

04 — Verify

Nothing closes until it's actually confirmed

A mission is marked resolved only once a webhook confirms the payment and the outcome is verified against real system state — never on the strength of an action having been sent.

04

Why it's safe to hand this money

The model has no path to unrestricted control over money. That holds regardless of how it's prompted, or what it "believes" is the right call.

Bounded by design

RESOLVE is never given open-ended permission to act. Every mission carries a hard, machine-checked spend ceiling.

Every action explainable

Every approval or block is written to an insert-only audit log — a full, replayable reason for every decision.

Nothing executes unchecked

The reasoning model proposes. A separate, plain, deterministic Authority Engine is the only thing that can approve.

Real payment rails

Every refund, payout, and recovery payment runs through Razorpay, confirmed by a signature-verified webhook — never assumed.

For merchants

Run your own Merchant Agent

A small, self-hostable service that holds your return policy and your own bounded spend ceiling, and settles disputes directly with RESOLVE — often in under a minute, instead of days of email back-and-forth. No Merchant Agent yet? RESOLVE falls back to structured, policy-aware correspondence automatically.
